brief.name: Fixture colonial pavilion hospital (invented)
brief.subject: fixture

sources.what: built 1912, opened 1924; 2,000 beds; Avenue Colonel Ebeya in Gombe; formerly Mama Yemo Hospital; eight operating suites rebuilt after 1997

brief.notes: History and bed count are sourced; the pavilion/ward layout is a typical-colonial-hospital estimate. A worn, busy public hospital in faded cream render.

style.vernacular: Huge river capital on flat low ground beside the Congo. Belgian-era grid and 1950s modernist blocks (white or cream concrete, brise-soleil, pilotis) in Gombe and Limete; vast self-built communes of 1-2 storey cement-block houses in painted render with rust or grey corrugated roofs; Mobutu-era monumental government and sport buildings; Chinese-built landmarks after 1990 (stadium, palaces). Sandy-red earth, oil palms and mango trees, and walls hand-painted in bright commercial colours.
style.ornament: Colonial 1950s tropical modernism (brise-soleil, concrete grilles, pilotis, curved canopies); Mobutu-era monumentalism and authenticite statuary; hand-painted advertising murals and telecom-coloured shopfronts; arched colonnades on older Belgian buildings.

sources.what: Koppen Aw flat low terrain; Belgian colonial grid, prefabricated Danish houses, 1950s two-storey housing and apartment blocks, Palace of the Nation, Academie des Beaux-Arts
colonial-era terminal by Leon Marcel Chapeaux with 2012 bronze-glass facade
